title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
authors: N. Shinn, F. Cassano, E. Berman, A. Gopinath, K. Narasimhan, S. Yao
before: An agent that failed a task simply failed and started over.
problem: Improving from failure normally means gradient updates, which is impossible at inference time.
breakthrough: Have the agent write a verbal post-mortem of its failure and keep it in memory for the next attempt.
why: Learning from experience without touching the weights, which became a standard pattern in agent design.
next: Memory and self-critique layers in agent frameworks and coding agents.
inherits: Episodic self-reflection as an agent's cheap substitute for training.
